# P9 paired campaign statistics and pipeline power on E-SYN

**ENGINEERING_ONLY.** Generated by `python -m paperc.power_validation`.

## Statistical decision

The paired unit is (node, instance seed, start configuration). Nested audit measurements first average within matched manager repetitions. Repetitions then average within a root. The fitted artifact is fixed within each test. Explicitly incomplete attempts are counted by arm and excluded as whole pairs. The analysis uses one-sided paired t superiority and the maximum of the two one-sided TOST p-values. Holm is applied across the declared nodes within each Q family, separately for superiority and TOST. Each uses α = 0.025. Unavailable nodes retain their Holm slots. Both statistical outcomes may hold. The stored paired intervals are unadjusted. The family decision uses Holm-adjusted p-values. An equivalence declaration additionally needs predeclared zero-effect power of at least 0.80.

## Known-variance Normal control

The one-candidate limit uses `n=128`, known SD 1 and symmetric margin 0.3. The simulation passes paired Normal draws through the same inference and family decision functions with known variance. The closed form integrates the Normal sample mean beyond the superiority bound or within the two TOST bounds.

| True effect | Exact superiority | MC superiority [95% MC CI] | Exact TOST | MC TOST [95% MC CI] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.000 | 0.0250 | 108/4096 [0.02, 0.03] | 0.8485 | 3440/4096 [0.83, 0.85] |
| 0.150 | 0.3963 | 1636/4096 [0.38, 0.41] | 0.3954 | 1638/4096 [0.38, 0.42] |

## End-to-end E-SYN simulation

12 independent repetitions each use two independently seeded synthetic nodes with the same short-budget E-SYN law. Each node recollects run-specific behaviour-mixture roots and N6 training forks, refits the P8 settings, screens support on separate roots, tunes each method on dev, selects the family members on dev, and then generates fresh paired test campaigns. The test uses the frozen selected artifact from the single prespecified fit seed of that repetition. The distributions across repetitions include variation from training and dev selection.

Per node there are 3072 training, 512 support and 600 dev roots. Test uses two disjoint blocks of 512 roots each. The 15 P4 logging components and P8 reward shaping and support rules carry over. Q1 selects among N3, N4 and N6 against N1. Q3 selects R0 or R1 against the dev-best of N4 and N6. Ties follow the declared method order. Training candidates that fail support are ineligible for dev selection.

The exact DP value is 0.002268128; the best same-horizon myopic value is 0.002180460. The E-SYN margin is 10% of their difference, δ = 0.000008767. The raw case uses fresh paired campaign contrasts, with common audit noise cancelling as in P8. For zero-effect planning, take two independent contrasts D and D′ for the selected artifacts and form (D − D′)/√2. The mean is exactly zero and the conditional variance is preserved. This also symmetrizes the distribution. The positive planning case adds 2δ to that contrast. The latter two are controlled test laws for planning rather than claims about the actual selected policies. The displayed TOST rates are statistical rejections, before the power gate.

The denominator includes attempts with missing selections or unresolved variance. The MC intervals are exact binomial intervals across independent pipeline replicates. Holm is recalculated jointly over the two nodes in each replicate, family and scenario.

The dev–test gap is descriptive. It includes method selection and finite test sampling. The limited synthetic replication and short horizon give no real-node sizing or equivalence declaration. The JSON retains the candidate decisions, selected policies, exact references and per-repetition tests.

Test references are [Holm (1979)](https://www.ime.usp.br/~abe/lista/pdf4R8xPVzCnX.pdf) and [Schuirmann (1987)](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01068419).
